samples.xml_description:
<module id="serial2parallel">
    <description>A series-parallel conversion circuit. Receives a serial input signal "din_serial" along with a control signal "din_valid" indicating the validity of the input data. Operates on the rising edge of the clock signal "clk". Synchronous design. Output dout_parallel stores 8-bit data, where the serial input values are sequentially placed from the most significant bit to the least significant bit. Output dout_valid indicates the validity of the output data.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="clk">Clock signal.</input>
        <input id="rst_n">Reset signal (active low).</input>
        <input id="din_serial">Serial input data.</input>
        <input id="din_valid">Validity signal for input data.</input>
        <output id="dout_parallel" width_description="[7:0]">Parallel output data (8 bits wide).</output>
        <output id="dout_valid">Validity signal for the output data.</output>
    </ports>
    <implementation>The module utilizes a 4-bit counter (cnt) to keep track of the number of serial input data bits received. Every eight din_serial input, dout_parallel will output. When all 8 serial data bits have been received, the valid output signal is set to 1, indicating that the parallel output data is valid. Otherwise, the valid output signal is set to 0, indicating that the parallel output data is not valid.</implementation>
</module>
